summary: Decision logs can become ceremonial, stale, selective, or politically sanitized. A long archive may preserve the appearance of rationale while the actual trade-offs remain in private conversations.

points.text: Research finds many ADRs begin directly in accepted state, bypassing alternatives and deliberation; such records document an outcome but not a reusable decision process.
If records are not linked to code and change triggers, old assumptions remain discoverable but misleading, increasing confidence in obsolete constraints.
Teams may avoid recording security weaknesses, interpersonal trade-offs, commercial constraints, or uncertainty, leaving the most important rationale outside the searchable archive.
Requiring an ADR for routine choices creates documentation queues and dilutes significant decisions among low-value records.
